You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — SunEdison Semiconductor Limited realized record, ~3-5-year horizon (fixed window ~2017-2019)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The fixed outcome window for this case is the
> ~2017-2019 record. Because the registrant was acquired and deregistered before that
> window opened, there is no post-closing public periodic report covering it; the terminal
> events are traced through the registrant's own SEC filings. This sub-dossier contains no
> information about how the earlier transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status across the outcome window
- The registrant's last annual report is the Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December
  31, 2015, filed March 8, 2016; no Form 10-K or other periodic report was filed for any
  period in the ~2017-2019 outcome window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001585854-16-000093, Form 10-K (FY2015)]
- On December 2, 2016 NASDAQ filed a Form 25 (notification of removal from listing and
  registration) effecting delisting of the ordinary shares and their deregistration under
  Section 12(b) of the Exchange Act. [SRC: SEC accession 0001354457-16-000569, Form 25-NSE]
- The registrant filed a Form 15-12B on December 5, 2016 to terminate registration of its
  ordinary shares and suspend its reporting obligations under Sections 13 and 15(d) of the
  Exchange Act. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-16-784713, Form 15-12B]

## Terminal event and change of control (realized record)
- Effective December 2, 2016, pursuant to an Implementation Agreement and a Scheme of
  Arrangement under Section 210 of the Singapore Companies Act, GWafers Singapore Pte. Ltd.
  (an entity of GlobalWafers Co., Ltd., a Republic of China / Taiwan company) "acquired all
  of the outstanding ordinary shares of the Company," and "the Company is an indirect wholly
  owned subsidiary of GWC." [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-16-784692, Form 8-K Item 2.01]
- Consideration: shareholders (other than the acquiror group) received "the right to receive
  US$12.00 per share in cash." [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-16-784692, Form 8-K Item 2.01]
- Leadership/organization at the change of control: "each member of the Company's board of
  directors resigned from the board," and three GWC-designated directors (Doris Hsiu-Lan Hsu,
  Mark Lynn England and Woo Heng Thong) were appointed; on December 2, 2016 "the employment
  of Shaker Sadasivam, President and Chief Executive Officer of the Company, was terminated." [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-16-784692, Form 8-K Item 5.02]
- Financing at the change of control: the 2014 senior secured credit agreement (as amended
  December 29, 2015) "was repaid in full and terminated," the MEMC Korea term loans with
  Shinhan Bank, Hana Bank and Korea Development Bank were "repaid in full and terminated,"
  and a new facility of up to $200.0 million guaranteed by GWC was entered by the Company's
  subsidiary. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-16-784692, Form 8-K Items 1.01, 1.02]

## Outcome coding (no-record rule)
- Because the registrant was acquired via scheme of arrangement and deregistered in December
  2016 — before the fixed ~2017-2019 outcome window opened — there is no separate public
  audited SEC record of its realized business trajectory within that window. The acquirer,
  GlobalWafers Co., Ltd., is a Taiwan-listed company and not a U.S. SEC registrant; no
  separate segment disclosure of the acquired business's post-acquisition trajectory was
  located in the retrieved public primaries. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-16-784692, Form 8-K Item 2.01] [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-16-784713, Form 15-12B]
- Accordingly the outcome for the ~2017-2019 window is coded **uncertain (no public
  record)**; any financial scalar for that window would require a primary filing that does
  not exist, and none is inferred here from an acquirer's consolidated results. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-16-784713, Form 15-12B]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- The traceable realized record ends with a change of control: the entity was acquired by
  GlobalWafers for US$12.00 per share cash effective December 2, 2016, its entire board
  resigned and its CEO was terminated the same day, its listing and SEC registration were
  terminated, and its closing-era credit facilities were repaid and replaced with an
  acquirer-guaranteed facility — after which no separate public periodic reporting exists for
  the ~2017-2019 window, so the post-closing outcome over that horizon is coded uncertain. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-16-784692, Form 8-K Items 1.01, 1.02, 2.01, 5.02] [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-16-784713, Form 15-12B]

[SLICE END]
